name: fix_python_mass_assignment
description: Fixes a mass-assignment privilege escalation: update_user copies every key from an untrusted body onto the user
prompts: update_user(user, data) in users.py applies an untrusted request body (data) to a User by doing setattr for EVERY key in data. That is a mass-assignment vulnerability: a request can set role='admin' to escalate privileges, or set any arbitrary attribute. Fix update_user to only apply an allowlist of user-editable fields - name and email - and ignore every other key (including role and any unknown attribute). Keep the User class and the update_user(user, data) signature.

test_setup_files.test_users.py:
from users import User, update_user


def test_updates_allowed_fields():
    user = update_user(User("Ada", "a@b.com"), {"name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@x.io"})
    assert user.name == "Ada Lovelace"
    assert user.email == "ada@x.io"


def test_ignores_role_escalation():
    user = update_user(User("Ada", "a@b.com"), {"name": "X", "role": "admin"})
    assert user.role == "user"
    assert user.name == "X"


def test_ignores_arbitrary_attributes():
    user = update_user(User("Ada", "a@b.com"), {"is_staff": True, "password_hash": "x"})
    assert not hasattr(user, "is_staff")
    assert not hasattr(user, "password_hash")
